question: Is the PTRACE reference itself double-run deterministic at every ladder rung? Any rung where it diverges from itself is disqualified as a golden.
method: Per rung, N=5 INDEPENDENT PAIRS. Each pair: two `--log info --log-file` captures under --strict, leading wall-clock timestamp stripped, compared byte-for-byte. This is the golden's own definition of identity, so the verdict binds to what the ratchet actually compares.
comparison_depth: INFO log (Detcore COMMIT + DETLOG records). NOT stdout-only.

A-ratchet-f89c69766.why: the SHA the prefix-depth ratchet captured its golden at

not_established: Set A's Z counts (23/52/53/182) differ from the ratchet doc's (14/43/44/16) because the ratchet's env and its exact fork/exec guest are not recorded in the doc; my Set A rungs approximate rather than reproduce them.
Set B used a debug build at the golden SHA, not the manifest's exact release binary (sha256 differs); the Z counts match the manifest exactly, which is the strongest available cross-check.

N=5 pairs bounds a flake rate loosely: 0/5 clean pairs leaves a ~45% one-sided 95% upper bound on a per-pair flake rate. IDENTICAL here means 'not observed to diverge in 5 pairs', not 'proven deterministic'.
